methodology.source: Actual git show bytes from each pinned commit, bundled with its own imported-texture-budget and foliage-mipmaps dependencies; no reconstructed baseline algorithm.
methodology.fixtures: Every authored fixture image is a 1024x512 scalar canvas double. Generated cases use real Three.js CanvasTexture wrappers; imported cases use real Texture wrappers with flipY=false and immutableAssetTexture=true. The budget is configured to 128 pixels and anisotropy 2. Each wrapper appears in both map and alphaMap material slots. The mixed case has four authored sources and six budget groups, including a scale-2 claim and a separate CPU-readback claim.
methodology.operations: Untimed separate proof processes use instrumented scalar canvas doubles, real Three.js 0.180.0 classes, duplicate map/alphaMap material slots and actual engine traversal. Counts are logical calls/version increments, not physical allocation or GPU work.
methodology.timing: Separate fresh Node child per variant per case. Only one child executes each sample; pair order alternates. Six default warmup pairs (96 fresh registrations per variant per case) precede twelve measured pairs (192 registrations per variant per case). All raw per-registration durations are retained.
methodology.timedBoundary: Only TextureBudget.register(root), including traversal, source/group ownership, stub canvas calls, wrapper disposal dispatch and version updates. The uninstrumented scalar canvas double does no rasterization, pixel copying or WebGL work.
outsideTiming: explicit GC before each multi-registration sample
methodology.nativeEvidence: Reuses committed w06d native results after validating target source hashes against candidate. This run does not rerun browser tests or compare baseline native pixels directly.
caveats: Both implementations already share budget Source storage. No GPU-allocation reduction is claimed.
Imported immutable images already drew once in the baseline; their measured improvement is repeated wrapper-update/traversal work.
Initial resize disposal-event counts increase when every acquired wrapper is invalidated together; these events are reported separately and do not count allocated GPU objects.
Registration microbenchmark on one Node/runtime/host. No browser/GPU duration, end-to-end frame time/FPS or GC/allocation-rate claim.
Elapsed timings include any incidental runtime pauses within register. CPU affinity, frequency and JIT tier are not controlled.

baseline.boundary: Instrumented scalar paint-propagation canvas double; no browser rasterization or GPU.

candidate.boundary: Instrumented scalar paint-propagation canvas double; no browser rasterization or GPU.
